revision: Cumulative authorized dirty WB-01..WB-16 worktree based on 0534135d877ec3679bb91ee0b4a68b71e174ff7a. docs/evidence/WB-16.dirty.diff records the complete worktree delta from that base, including untracked implementation/tests and the final task/evidence records, while excluding only the diff file itself. No commit or push was made.
environment: macOS 26.4.1 arm64, Macmini9,1; Neovim 0.11.7 minimum and 0.12.4 current/host; Python 3.14.6, mini.test 0.16.0, pynvim 0.6.0, msgpack 1.1.1. Native diagnostics used Neovim's vim.diagnostic API; LSP detach used the deterministic local stdio fake server. Linux and cold-cache startup were unavailable/not measured.
summary: Implemented a shared native diagnostics provider with scoped DiagnosticChanged/BufWipeout listeners and idempotent consumer leases; Problems groups diagnostics by root/file/namespace with exact severity/source/root filters, safe location navigation, explicit reported-only/incomplete coverage, and empty-state wording that never claims the workspace is clean. Files now aggregates changed-resource badges incrementally. Tests cover sibling-namespace preservation, diagnostic deletion, native LSP detach, unrelated roots, unnamed buffers, no-diagnostic state, shared Files/Problems leases, foreign autocmd preservation, and closing all consumers without clearing editor diagnostics. Added a keyboard-driven Problems RPC-grid journey to test-e2e. No host startup, root configuration, or Nix wiring changed.

gates.command: make check-ownership; inspect docs/tasks.json#WB-16 ownership, provider/controller boundaries and resource disposal
gates.result: WB-16 is within the declared workbench providers/controllers/tests/Makefile paths. The Diagnostics provider owns one augroup with DiagnosticChanged and BufWipeout handlers only while at least one lease is active; the last release removes both handlers and the in-memory projection without resetting Neovim diagnostics. Problems owns each tab session, action registration, view, and lease; Files owns its separate badge lease and per-resource/ancestor counts. Navigation is injected through the shared service. Manual boundary review found no provider-to-UI dependency. The ownership check passed for all 29 Lua modules; the cumulative diff records every dirty and untracked file. No root host mappings, init bootstrap, or Nix files changed.

All 108 mini.test cases passed on both Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4. All 21 Python integration/plan tests passed, and scripts/check_plan.py reported valid planning structure. The runtime suite includes provider snapshots and namespace provenance, incremental update after one namespace resets, complete deletion, fake native-LSP diagnostic publication/detach, Problems severity/source/root filtering and navigation/return, incomplete empty state, shared Files/Problems hooks, badge updates, diagnostic preservation, and foreign-autocmd preservation.

gates.command: WORKBENCH_TEST_FILE=tests/runtime/test_diagnostics.lua make test; inspect deletion, detach, root filtering, empty/incomplete coverage, shared leases and disposal assertions
gates.result: All six focused diagnostic cases passed on both Neovim versions. Clearing one native namespace retains the sibling namespace; clearing the final diagnostic removes the URI report. Detaching the fake native LSP client removes its report while the active provider listener remains live. Unnamed and unrelated-root buffers are excluded. With no diagnostics, Problems explicitly reports unknown completeness and does not say the workspace is clean. Files and Problems share one provider group; closing one keeps the other's listener active, and closing the last removes the group while editor diagnostics and a foreign DiagnosticChanged autocmd remain intact.

The real ext_linegrid/RPC journey passed at all four grid sizes on Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4. It uses native vim.diagnostic.set data and keyboard input to open Problems through the shared action palette, expand a file, observe a live DiagnosticChanged update, filter severity/source/root, open a selected reported location, return to origin, and close. Every run reported reported-only coverage, preserved all three native diagnostics after close, navigated to line 2 column 3, and ended with zero leases and zero provider hooks. The same command is wired into the Makefile test-e2e target.

gates.command: .test-deps/venv/bin/python bench/startup.py --runs 20 --nvim nvim; compare against the WB-15 same-host baseline and inspect WB-16 DiagnosticChanged-to-render samples
gates.result: On the same warm Macmini9,1/Nvim 0.12.4 host, the repeat 20-pair run measured host startup marker p50/p95 44.297/45.034 ms versus the prior baseline 43.799/45.113 ms; median delta was +0.498 ms and both medians remain well below the 150 ms limit. UI first-frame p50/p95 was 57.703/60.390 ms versus 57.553/60.553 ms; first-input state was 1.836/1.936 ms versus 1.808/1.849 ms. The repeat removed transient outliers from the first after-run (p95 68.406 ms), so that tail was investigated rather than hidden. Startup profiles show existing host vim.lsp, themekit, and autoconf costs; the new Diagnostics provider/controller are not loaded on startup and no startup/bootstrap files changed. Across the eight final RPC-grid samples, native DiagnosticChanged-to-render measured 1.688–2.307 ms. These are warm local results; cold cache and Linux were not measured.
